items.summary:
Donald Trump hails Huang as a ‘great patriot and national treasure’ after his surprise reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO

  • US reactions to Jensen Huang return – US politics live

  • Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO

Shares in UK housebuilder Crest Nicholson have slumped by a quarter, to a record low, after the company issued a profits warning this morning.

Full year completions were 1,353, at the bottom end of the Group’s previous guidance range of 1,350 to 1,400 completions.

The warning has hammered Crest Nicholson shares, which have lost more than a quarter of their value this morning, currently trading down over 30%. The brutal sell-off is also weighing on the wider sector, dragging peers like Barratt Redrow, Persimmon, Vistry and Bellway into the red.

Today’s update suggests that weakness in the housing market is no longer confined to first-time buyers. Crest Nicholson is predominantly exposed to the mid-premium family housing market, and the sharp deterioration in sales rates indicates that more affluent upsizers are also becoming increasingly cautious amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO was great for the tech elite – and not so great for the rest of us | Steven Greenhouse
items.summary:
The company’s co-founders are now wildly rich, while countless Americans face AI-driven threats to their jobs and fears of a stock bubble

The sultans of Silicon Valley and the wizards of Wall Street rejoiced this week when Anthropic raised an eye-popping $81bn in the largest initial public offering in history. They saw the AI company’s IPO as a gung-ho affirmation of Silicon Valley’s and Wall Street’s marriage of technology and capitalism.

For many employees at the company that developed Claude, the public offering must have been a thing of dreams. With the IPO valuing Anthropic at $1.5tn, the company’s seven co-founders each came away with stakes worth about $20bn, while, by one estimate, 600 of Anthropic’s more than 5,000 employees will have holdings topping $100m and 2,800 others will have shares worth more than $10m.

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.

Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

items.title: Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry
items.summary:
A record breaking IPO has raised billions for the AI frontier lab – but experts say the coming months could prove bumpy, as the industry faces a variety of challenges

  • Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO

In the end, Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO more than lived up to the hype. The market’s embrace of one of the AI industry’s most talked about companies has resulted in the maker of the Claude chatbot becoming one of the world’s most valuable firms after just one day of trading.

With many of the company’s founders, investors and employees now worth billions of dollars – and demand for the company’s stock remaining resilient – attention now turns to the stability of the wider market, and the global headwinds that experts say could threaten the AI industry over the coming months.

Continue reading...
items.t: Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry

items.title: Anthropic shares end first day of trading at $97 as Wall Street closes sharply lower – as it happened
items.summary:
All ⁠three major US stock indexes ⁠ended the session ​sharply lower after record-breaking IPO by maker behind AI agent Claude

  • Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation

  • Protesters rally in New York and San Francisco

  • Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

Anthropic needs to grow into its $1.5tn valuation, argues Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB:

Anthropic’s triumphant IPO and its trillion dollar plus valuation is more typical of a mature company that has a history of strong fundamentals. Anthropic could not be more different. It has generated strong revenue growth, but only in the short term, added to this, it is still unprofitable.

Anthropic is another major tech company that requires investors to have a lot of faith about the future generation of revenues based on technology that will change the world. It seems like plenty are willing to give it that faith, and it is having a huge impact on the broader market today.

items.title: Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO
items.summary:
AI startup and Claude chatbot maker became one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded businesses with final share price of $97

  • Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry

Anthropic closed its first day of trading on the US stock market about 17% higher than its initial public offering price. At the close of market on Thursday, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn total market capitalization, $1.75tn fully diluted.

While the final share value was higher than the IPO price of $83, it marked a dip from an early high of $111.50. The firm’s shares initially soared 34% when trading got under way on its US market debut on Thursday, valuing the company at more than $2tn. Nonetheless, Anthropic’s ranked among the biggest stock market flotations in history. The artificial intelligence startup, founded in 2021, became one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world.

items.title: Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?
items.summary:
The company counts physicists, a former journalist and an associate of the pope among its guiding lights

The paper fortunes of Anthropic’s seven co-founders reached a total of more than $180bn on Thursday as shares in their company started trading at a price ahead of expectations.

The opening price of $111.50 (£85) per share valued the entrepreneurs’ stakes – including the chief executive, Dario Amodei, and his sister Daniela – at between $26.5bn and $27bn each. The founders have pledged to donate 80% of their shareholdings in Anthropic to philanthropic causes, which would equate to about $150bn at the current share price.

items.title: Anthropic keeps the AI party swinging, but the atmosphere is bubbly | Nils Pratley
items.summary:
Can the newly listed AI company really be worth $2tn? Anyone who remembers the late 1990s has good reason to ask

Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company.

From the point of view of the promoters, the result was as good as it gets. The final pricing for the shares at $83 apiece was meaningfully higher than the indicated range of $70 to $78, but still left room for a big initial “pop”. There were positive vibes all round – especially for the battalion of investment banks collecting $550m of underwriting fees.

items.title: Anthropic sets share price at $83 for stock market debut, above expected range
items.summary:
Artificial intelligence firm positioned for one of the biggest IPOs in history, with trading slated to begin Thursday

Anthropic set the share price for its debut on the US stock market at $83 on Wednesday, positioning the artificial intelligence company for one of the biggest initial public offerings in history. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange.

The pricing is above Anthropic’s earlier estimates. Last week, the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, set its preliminary share price at $70 to $78. With all shares counted, those prices put Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) from $1.26tn to $1.41tn. Elon Musk’s SpaceX debuted on Wall Street in June with the biggest market offering ever at $1.77tn. With Anthropic setting its share price at $83, it could now surpass SpaceX.

Continue reading...
items.t: Anthropic sets share price at $83 for stock market debut, above expected range
